original_question: Which types of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy might show decreased dystrophin levels on immunohistochemical testing, despite lacking mutations in the dystrophin gene?

final_qi.question: Which types of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy might show decreased dystrophin levels on immunohistochemical testing, despite lacking mutations in the dystrophin gene?
final_qi.search_keyword: limb-girdle muscular dystrophy decreased dystrophin levels immunohistochemical testing
final_qi.long_answer: Sarcoglycanopathies, which are forms of limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy caused by mutations in one of the sarcoglycan genes (such as LGMD2C, LGMD2D, LGMD2E, and LGMD2F), may show decreased dystrophin levels on immunohistochemical testing. Even though the dystrophin gene itself is not mutated in these cases, disruption of the sarcoglycan complex can lead to secondary reductions in dystrophin expression. This immunohistochemical finding can therefore be observed as a helpful diagnostic clue in sarcoglycan-deficient forms of LGMD.
